findings.title: markSubmitting accepts an already-'submitting' row, so concurrent runners can each submit the same effect once
findings.body: `LiveEffectStore.markSubmitting` runs `UPDATE ... WHERE state = 'prepared'` and then only post-checks that the re-read row has `state === 'submitting'`. It never verifies that this call performed the prepared→submitting transition (the `.run()` result's `changes` count is discarded). If two invocations of `runRecoverableEffect` race on the same effect key (two processes sharing the WAL database, or interleaved async calls in one process), both pass `prepare`, both see `state === 'prepared'` in their snapshot, both reconcile 'absent', and then both calls to `markSubmitting` succeed — the second one as a no-op UPDATE whose post-check still observes `state = 'submitting'`. Both then call `adapter.submit`, producing two external submissions under one effect key. This is outside the pure crash/restart scenarios the interruption tests cover (after a real restart there is no concurrent peer), so the round-002 claim 'durable submission-attempt marker prevents duplicate external submission after restart' holds as literally stated; but the marker does not make the submit gate single-winner, and the in-scope threat list includes direct API misuse and restart-caused duplicate effects. Minimal fix: capture the `changes` count from `.run()` and throw unless exactly one row transitioned (bun:sqlite's `Statement.run` returns `{ changes, lastInsertRowid }`), making the prepared→submitting transition a compare-and-swap. A small test driving two interleaved `runRecoverableEffect` calls on one key would pin the behavior.

overall_explanation: All four round-001 corrections are verifiably implemented in the bundle. (1) Directory payload stability: `projectDirectorySummary` sets `catalogObservedAt` from the listing's signed `presentedAt`, so the keyed directory payload is byte-stable across verification clocks; `test/live/demos-listing.test.ts` replays the full publication with `nowMs + 1` and asserts identical results with no new submissions. (2) Durable submission-attempt marker: `runRecoverableEffect` calls `store.markSubmitting` (state 'prepared' → 'submitting', persisted via an autocommit registered atomic-write site) before `adapter.submit`; on a later run with the row in 'submitting', an 'absent' reconciliation throws 'refusing to resubmit' (fail closed), while a positive reconciliation flows through `observe` (whose SQL accepts 'submitting') to commit — the 'never resubmits an attempted effect' test proves exactly one submission across repeated absence. (3) Already-observed rows: the runner's early path commits an 'observed' intent and returns the stored result without touching the adapter; the 'before-commit' interruption case exercises it. (4) Allow-list gating: the runner rejects non-admitted kinds before `prepare`, and the test asserts no row is persisted. (5) The import-boundary verifier now recursively scans the entire `src/` tree (including `src/index.ts`) for the SDK specifier and separately asserts the adapter's exact-commit pin check. (6) Coherence: schema v25 adds `live_effect_intents` with STRICT typing and state/ref CHECK invariants matching every store transition; the four registry rows, autocommit set, expectation line numbers (effect-store.ts:46/82/68/94), interruption driver overrides (the before-commit case exercises all four sites), user_version 25 test updates, provenance hashes for every touched file, and docs all agree. The `rigInventory` historical-tag mode is fail-closed (unresolvable tag falls back to the working tree and mismatches; `git show` failure throws), and the release test pins both the tagged digest and its divergence from the working tree. The single residual finding — `markSubmitting` not enforcing a single-winner transition under concurrent invocation — is a narrow edge outside the restart-focused protected claims and does not block landing. No secret leakage, injection, or trust-boundary regression found; HTTPS is enforced at both adapter boundaries and git subprocesses use argument arrays.
